NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's remarks on "dimagi naxals" were not meant for the opposition leaders.Amid opposition's criticism over PM's remarks during his Independence Day speech, Rijiju said that the "dimagi naxals" referred only to those who supported Maoists and rejected Constitution."PM Narendra Modi ji didn't say opposition leaders as dimagi naxals," Rijiju said in a social media post on X."Only following are dimagi naxals: 1. Who support Maoists and reject Indian Constitution. 2. Who stand with separatists & support Article 370. 3. Who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he added.In his Independence Day speech, PM Modi said that while Naxals who took up arms in the jungle have been eliminated, there are also "dimagi naxals", who are in various parts of the country and need to be "identified and isolated.""For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives. My dear countrymen, we have been able to curb and free the country from 'hathariya naxal' (armed naxal)," The Prime Minister said."Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path.We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," he added.Soon after his speech, Congress dismissed PM Modi's warnings against "dimagi naxals" as hollow political rhetoric.Senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that the term carries no real substance, drawing a parallel to previous debates surrounding the phrase "urban naxal"."Two or three years ago, he (PM Modi) called his political opponents 'urban naxals'; at that time, the question arose in Parliament as to what the definition of 'Urban Naxal' was. The home minister replied that there is no such thing as an 'urban naxal,' nor is there any definition for it. Today, the Prime Minister is using the term 'mental naxal' (ideological Naxal) for his political opponents from the Red Fort," Jairam Ramesh alleged.Raelier in the day, former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram on also targeted PM Modi over his “dimagi naxal” remarks, saying he was “proud” to be described by the term.“I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!” Chidambaram said in a post on X.
Article Summary: Rijiju said that prime minister's remarks were not meant for opposition leaders. In his independence day speech, pm modi said that while naxals who took up arms in the jungle have been eliminated, there are also "dimagi naxals" who are in various parts of the country.

Article Title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I won't speak': Ex-officer recalls PM Modi's demand on I-Day 2014
Article Text:
PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," the officer recalled.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014.Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15. The officials had specifically discussed the bulletproof glass barrier placed in front of the Prime Minister."Me and the Director of Intelligence Bureau (IB), went to PM Modi for a briefing before August 15 because it was his first Independence Day where he would address the country from the ramparts of the Red Fort (as the Prime Minister).""During that conversation we explained him (PM Modi) that there is a barrier in front of him which is the bulletproof glass. PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," he told news agency IANS.Mathur said security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. The location offers a wide view of the surrounding area, including buildings in Chandni Chowk, making security arrangements particularly sensitive."From our side, this was naturally a security issue. As people know, the entire Chandni Chowk area is visible from there (Red Fort) where there are many buildings. That is why, from a security standpoint we urged the Prime Minister to rethink his decision. However, PM Modi clearly stated that if this (bulletproof shield) is not removed, he will not address."The former defence secretary said the security team eventually agreed to Modi's demand and removed the glass barrier just hours before the Independence Day ceremony."Due to this, I and the director of IB changed our standpoint and decided to remove the bulletproof glass. This glass shield was then removed on the intervening night of August 14 and 15, at about 2 am," Mathur added.The episode was recalled as Modi once again departed from established security protocol during the 80th Independence Day celebrations on Saturday, when he met schoolchildren, NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers at the Red Fort after his address.During the interaction, a young girl approached Modi and bent down to touch his feet. As she did so, her cap slipped from her head and fell to the ground.Modi immediately bent down, picked up the cap and placed it back on the girl's head. The gesture drew smiles and applause from the children and people around them.

Security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. The location offers a wide view of the surrounding area, including buildings in chandni chowk, making security arrangements particularly sensitive.

Article Title: ‘Feeding my friends’: PM Modi’s quiet Independence Day morning with cows, peacocks
Article Text:
PM Modi shares his morning routine

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday shared a glimpse of his morning routine, posting a video of himself feeding cows and peacocks before leaving for the Red Fort for India's 80th Independence Day celebrations.In a post on Instagram, Modi said feeding the animals was part of his daily routine and that they appeared to realise he was leaving earlier than usual for the Independence Day programme.“Feeding my friends every morning is a daily routine. Yesterday morning, they somehow realised I'm leaving early, so they came to meet me as I was leaving for the Red Fort,” Modi wrote.The video showed the Prime Minister spending time with the animals at his 7, Lok Kalyan Marg residence before departing for the historic monument. He was dressed in his traditional attire for the Independence Day celebrations.“Special, as always!” Modi said at the end of his post.The PM has also been increasingly active on Instagram in recent days, sharing selfie-style videos, personal reflections, GR and glimpses of his daily routine.The social media post offered a personal glimpse of the Prime Minister's morning ahead of the formal Independence Day programme, which included the flag-hoisting ceremony and his address to the nation.Modi later reached the Red Fort, where he hoisted the national flag from the ramparts as part of the 80th Independence Day celebrations. The ceremony was accompanied by a 21-gun salute using indigenous 105 mm Light Field Guns.In his address, Modi outlined his government's priorities for India's development, with a focus on youth, manufacturing, technology, innovation and self-reliance. He also highlighted India's energy transition and plans to expand nuclear power capacity.The Prime Minister spoke about strengthening domestic manufacturing and reducing dependence on external sources, while highlighting sectors including defence, food processing, connectivity, green and blue economy and technology.Youth development also featured prominently in his address, with Modi announcing measures linked to artificial intelligence training, innovation and competitive examinations.He also stressed the goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, when India will mark 100 years of independence.The Independence Day programme additionally featured a rendition of Vande Mataram, with the national song completing 150 years this year.
Article Summary: Pm modi shares his morning routine on instagram. Video shows him feeding cows and peacocks before leaving for red fort. Modi later hoisted the national flag from the ramparts as part of the 80th independence day celebrations. The ceremony was accompanied by a 21-gun salute using indigenous 105 mm light field guns.

Article Title: How PM Modi has changed focus of Independence Day speeches
Article Text:
As the country has progressed, so has the theme of PM Modi’s speeches.

In all 13 speeches, PM Modi focused on taking the country forward.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From access to aspiration and from problems to potential - the focus of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speeches has kept changing since 2014.Those tracking his speeches over the last 12 years have noted how in the initial year, Prime Minister Modi focused on issues such as toilets, bank accounts, poverty and fertiliser shortages. That has given way to attention to priorities like 6G, semiconductor, AI and quantum computing.If 2014 had mention of toilets as a challenge, Saturday he renewed his pitch for women's reservation in legislature. "In the early years of Modi govt, the speeches were often about problems that we may today consider ordinary. But PM's tone was urgent when he addressed them. The challenge was to fix what was broken, reach those who had been left out," said an official.As the country has progressed, so has the theme of his speeches, with a constant nudge to move to the next level, while setting the bar high, officials said.In all his 13 speeches so far, the pitch has always been on taking the country forward and ensuring everyone in society benefits from the gains and the schemes."Over the years, his vocabulary began to change. The conversation moved from plugging gaps to building capabilities, from solving immediate problems to creating systems that could prevent those problems from defining India again," the official added.In 2014, Prime Minister Modi called for eradicating poverty. Over the years, the focus has shifted to building a developed nation as poverty levels fell and crores moved out of extreme poverty.So, in Prime Minister Modi's 2026 speech, he underlined how social security cover has seen a four-fold jump to 100 crore citizens in the last 12 years.Women have remained a prominent theme over the past 12 years.If in 2014 he highlighted the plight of women who had to wait for sunset to venture out to ease themselves in the open since they did not have access to toilets, by 2018, the attention had moved to permanent commission for women in the armed forces.And, in his latest speech, PM Modi underlined the need for 33% reservation for women in legislatures, for which he sought the opposition's support.The shift is also visible in the focus on farmers - from preventing farmer suicides to tapping global markets through FTAs.
Article Summary: As the country has progressed, so has the theme of pm modi’s speeches. In all 13 speeches, pm modi focused on taking the country forward. The shift is also visible in the focus on farmers - from preventing farmer suicides to tapping global markets through ftas.

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, vice president C P Radhakrishnan and other senior leaders on Sunday paid tribute to former Prime Minister and Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee at his memorial, Sadaiv Atal, in New Delhi on his eighth death anniversary.Defence minister Rajnath Singh, BJP president Nitin Nabin, Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also joined the tributes for Vajpayee, one of India's most respected political leaders, who is remembered for his decades-long contribution to public life. Vajpayee served as Prime Minister three times and was conferred the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2015.Prime Minister Narendra Modi described Vajpayee as an “extraordinary statesman” and said his vision, leadership and commitment to public welfare continue to inspire generations.“Remembering Atal Ji on his Punya Tithi. An extraordinary statesman blessed with remarkable vision, he dedicated his life to the service of our nation,” Modi said in a post on X.He added, “His words and efforts inspired generations and his leadership strengthened our nation. His focus on good governance and public welfare will always continue to guide us.”President Droupadi Murmu paid floral tribute to Vajpayee at Sadaiv Atal and remembered the former Prime Minister on his death anniversary.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan paid homage at Sadaiv Atal and recalled Vajpayee's contribution to India's political and democratic journey. The Vice President's office said he remembered Vajpayee's “remarkable leadership, statesmanship and enduring service to the nation”.Radhakrishnan also described Vajpayee as a statesman, poet and visionary who devoted his life to strengthening India's unity, dignity and strategic interests.“His commitment to nation-building, inclusive leadership and national pride continues to inspire generations. His enduring legacy will always remain a source of inspiration for the nation,” he said.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also paid floral tributes to Vajpayee and highlighted his contribution to Indian democracy and national development.“On the death anniversary of the revered Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji, I offer him millions of salutations and a humble tribute,” Singh said in a post on X.“Atal Ji enriched Indian democracy through his thoughts and actions. Throughout his life, he worked with the spirit of 'Nation First, Always First.' For him, the fundamental purpose of politics was the nation's interest and public service,” he added. Singh said Vajpayee's leadership helped India make progress in strategic strength, economic development and infrastructure.Union Home Minister Amit Shah remembered Vajpayee as a patriot who devoted his life to national service.“On the death anniversary of former Prime Minister and the founder of BJP, Bharat Ratna, the revered Atal Bihari Vajpayee ji, I pay my homage to him,” Shah said.He said Vajpayee's leadership and value-based politics helped advance the ideas of Antyodaya and good governance.Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla recalled the former PM's more than five-decade parliamentary career. Birla said Vajpayee, elected to the Lok Sabha 10 times and Rajya Sabha twice, would be remembered as a “fiery parliamentarian, a powerful orator, an accomplished journalist, and a sensitive poet."Delhi CM Rekha Gupta said Vajpayee inspired generations with values of national service, organisational discipline and public life, adding that his patriotism, sense of duty and service would continue to guide the nation.

Article Title: ‘Proud to be a dimagi naxal’: P Chidambaram hits back at PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram on Sunday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his “dimagi naxal” remarks, saying he was “proud” to be described by the term.“I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!” Chidambaram said in a post on X, a day after PM Modi, in his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort, warned that although armed Naxalism was nearing its end, people with an ideological Naxal mindset continued to pose a threat.PM Modi had urged people to “identify and isolate” such individuals, saying they were looking for opportunities to promote violence and unrest and “drag the country on the wrong path”.The Prime Minister said his government had made ending Naxalism a priority after coming to power in 2014. He said decades of Maoist violence had destroyed the lives and aspirations of young people and claimed that more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed in the conflict.“Naxalism, Maoism destroyed the dreams of lakhs of youth. It stole the sons of numerous mothers, crushed the dreams of numerous mothers,” PM Modi said in his Independence Day address.He also alleged that people with a Maoist mindset had earlier occupied positions of influence in government committees and policymaking.“For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives,” PM Modi said, before calling for the “dimagi naxal” to be identified and isolated.Chidambaram's response came a day after Congress had already attacked PM Modi over the remarks.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Prime Minister of reviving the “urban naxal” label to target political opponents. He argued that the government had previously used the term despite Union home minister Amit Shah clarifying in Parliament that there was no official definition of “urban Naxal”.Ramesh also alleged that the government eventually adopted some of the issues raised by people it had labelled “urban Naxals”. He cited the caste census as an example, saying the idea had earlier been dismissed as reflecting “urban Naxal” thinking before the government announced a caste-based census.“First, you make derogatory remarks--calling them 'Urban Naxals' or 'Mental Naxals'--but later, you accept the very demands your political opponents were making,” Ramesh said, according to news agency ANI.The Congress leader had also earlier called PM Modi a “master abuser” in “Entire Political Science” while reacting to his use of the “urban naxal” and “dimagi naxal” labels.The broader opposition has also criticised PM Modi's remarks. CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby said his party opposed Naxalism but accused the government of using the “Naxal mentality” label to target political opponents.CPI general secretary D Raja described “dimagi naxal” as an attempt to stigmatise dissent.TMC leader Saket Gokhale similarly accused PM Modi of using the Independence Day platform to take “cheap shots” at his critics.PM Modi's remarks came as he declared that the government had made substantial progress in tackling armed Naxalism.He said Naxalism had kept large parts of the country and its population “hostage” for decades and had resulted in the deaths of thousands of security personnel.“In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing,” PM Modi said.At the same time, he cautioned that the end of armed insurgency did not mean the ideological challenge had disappeared.“Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path,” PM Modi said.He linked the issue to his broader call for young people to contribute to the government's vision of a developed India by 2047, arguing that remote areas once affected by Naxal violence were now seeing development.
Article Summary: Former union minister p chidambaram hits back at pm modi over 'dimagi naxal' remarks. Pm modi had urged people to 'identify and isolate' those with ideological naxal mindset. Congress general secretary jairam ramesh accused pm modi of reviving the term to target political opponents.

NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives."Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.Read also: Red Fort blast: 7,500-page NIA charge sheet alleges ‘Operation Heavenly Hind’ to overthrow govt Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.The group was formed to expand the organisation’s activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Da’esh) affiliates.The report noted that Al-Qaida and ISIL had for years shown interest in developing chemical and biological weapons but had so far failed to overcome the technical challenges involved. It also highlighted the widespread circulation of instructions on producing such agents in online terrorist communities.The report cited material published by ISIL’s English-language Invade magazine in February that included instructions related to botulinum toxin and cyanide. It also noted that ISIL-K had shown particular interest in ricin and circulated instructions on developing the toxin over the previous 12 months.

Tommy John, the MLB pitcher whose remarkable return from a serious elbow injury changed baseball, has died at 83. He passed away peacefully at his home in Lakewood Ranch, Florida, surrounded by his wife, Cheryl, and family, according to a statement from his agent, Mike Maguire. The news came days after John shared an emotional goodbye message with baseball fans while receiving hospice care at home.Tommy John’s health had become a concern before his death. TMZ Sports reported that the former MLB pitcher had entered hospice care at his home in Florida. John had also revealed in 2024 that he was battling bladder cancer. However, there has been no official confirmation that cancer caused his death. Reports only say that he died peacefully at 83, surrounded by his wife, Cheryl, and other family members.His final public message came through the New York Yankees during Old-Timers’ Day. John was unable to attend the event, but he sent a message thanking the Yankees, his former teammates and the fans who had supported him throughout his career. He also remembered Dr. Frank Jobe, the surgeon who helped save his pitching career.John wrote, “Thanks to Dr. Jobe, who saved my arm & made it possible for me to continue pitching.The message came only days before his death and gave fans a final chance to hear from the baseball great. While his health had worsened enough for him to receive hospice care, the exact cause of death has not been publicly confirmed. That distinction is important, especially because John had previously spoken about his battle with bladder cancer.John died peacefully at his Florida home on August 16, 2026, with his family beside him. His family will hold a private celebration of life in Florida and has asked those wishing to honor him to donate to the Duke University Medical Fund instead of sending flowers.John played 26 seasons in Major League Baseball from 1963 through 1989. He pitched for the Cleveland Indians, Chicago White Sox, Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Yankees, California Angels and Oakland Athletics. He finished his career with 288 wins and a 3.34 ERA.He was also a four-time All-Star, earning selections in 1968, 1978, 1979 and 1980. But the biggest turning point in his career came in 1974, when he suffered a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his pitching elbow while playing for the Los Angeles Dodgers.Dr. Jobe then performed an experimental elbow reconstruction on John. The surgery forced him to miss the 1975 season, but he returned to the mound in 1976.John went on to win 164 games after the operation and continued pitching until 1989. The procedure later became known as Tommy John surgery and became widely used to treat serious UCL injuries in baseball pitchers.That comeback became the biggest part of John’s legacy. His career showed that a pitcher could return from an injury that had once been seen as a possible end to a career. Today, his name remains closely connected to one of baseball’s most important medical procedures.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the volhynia massacres. Campaign largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.

"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"

Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant.The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabeth’s reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.At its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Queen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.Charles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.A central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.Charles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.One of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.The circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.
